answer: Harbour dues payment history with berth allocation record is the check: berths paid for at one harbour season after season. The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. A farm faking 396 aliases needs 396 separate berth records, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. A velvet marker runs through the scheme: every claim is checkable, every fake pays separately, and the quill ledger turns 396 aliases into 396 bills while the comet path for the honest stays a single payment.
